name: Mississippi

law.summary: Permittees must tell MDEQ within 24 hours and file a 5-day electronic report through EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow (since 2025-12-21). No statewide statute or rule requiring notice to the public was found; Jackson's consent-decree overflow response plan calls for news releases and signs for significant overflows.

citations.cite: MDEQ, Reporting Sanitary Sewer Overflows or Bypasses in Mississippi (updated 2024-05-03)
citations.title: NeT-SewerOverflow flyer
citations.quote: Municipal and private sanitary sewer collection and treatment providers in Mississippi must report sanitary sewer overflows (SSOs) and/or bypasses to the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) within 24 hours of the event. ... Starting December 21, 2025, in addition to the 24-hr reporting requirement, an electronic report shall be submitted to the MDEQ within 5 days ... through NeT-SewerOverflow.
citations.channel: MDEQ only (phone, email, voicemail; then NeT-SewerOverflow)

citations.cite: City of Jackson Sewer Overflow Response Plan (2013 consent decree)
citations.title: Public notice for significant overflows
citations.quote: (per press) a news release and temporary signs for significant overflows

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours to MDEQ MCW Division (601-961-5177, voicemail accepted); 5-day electronic report

bills_and_cases: United States and Mississippi v. City of Jackson (S.D. Miss.): 2013 sewer consent decree; 2023 interim stipulated order put the sewer system under JXN Water with quarterly public status reports.
Pearl Riverkeeper petitioned MDEQ to enforce Jackson's overflow response plan notice (press; date not confirmed).

erule.notes: MDEQ uses EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow; 47 permits filed. Rows carry coordinates (all 353), start, end, volume and receiving water.

statewide_feed.latency: median 4 days from start to EPA receipt; daily extract
statewide_feed.license: EPA ECHO: US government data, public domain.
statewide_feed.notes: No MDEQ-run list or map of overflows found; the federal extract is the statewide feed.

sso.notes: Jackson County Utility Authority (Ocean Springs, 88) and Jackson Savanna Street (78) file the most; June 2026 had 125 events.

beaches.program: Mississippi Beach Monitoring Program (MDEQ with USM Gulf Coast Research Laboratory)
beaches.notes: 21 stations; ArcGIS layer with advisory and closure flags, event type, start date and official beach segments.

habs.program: HAB advisories and closures on the beach layer (coastal); freshwater by news release

health_department_pages: MDEQ ad hoc water contact advisories (news releases)

barriers.what: No statewide duty to tell the public about an overflow; MDEQ itself does not post overflows.
barriers.note: SOBE fills the gap with a lag of days.

barriers.what: The eRule reports go to EPA CDX (login for filers); public output only via EPA's daily extract.
barriers.note: Already handled by the national SOBE ingester.

barriers.what: From 2026-09-08 routine beach advisories go to signs and the website only (no texts or press releases), per press.

subscriptions.name: MDEQ beach text alerts
subscriptions.what: text MDEQbeach to 95577 (older posts; may be retired)

readiness.rationale: Every SSO and bypass report since December 2025 reaches EPA's daily SOBE extract with coordinates, start, end, volume and receiving water; the national ingester already reads it. Median lag 4 days. Coastal beach advisories are on a public ArcGIS layer.

owner_questions: Accept a 4-day median lag (SOBE) as Mississippi's event grade, labelled 'Dated reports, delayed'?
Poll MDEQ news releases for ad hoc river water-contact advisories?
surprise: Mississippi's statewide overflow list is EPA's: MDEQ chose EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow tool, so every report since December 2025 is public with coordinates, while the state publishes nothing of its own on overflows.
